newsitem.title: USA: Washington Gov. reviews $19 bln state budget plan.
newsitem.headline: Washington Gov. reviews $19 bln state budget plan.

text.p: Washington Gov. Gary Locke on Monday began to review the state legislature's $19 billion budget proposal, approved by the Republican-controlled Senate after a heated weekend battle with Democrats.
Republican lawmakers praised the two-year spending plan -- approved by the state Senate on Saturday night -- as a model of prudence and fiscal restraint.
The budget includes about $400 million in tax cuts. Two-thirds of the tax reductions accrue to various types of businesses while the other one-third would benefit homeowners in the state.
The Republican spending plan also calls for a record state budget reserve of about $500 million.
The budget "has the overall lowest rate of growth in state spending in more than a decade," said state Rep. Mark Schoesler, a Republican. "That's progress."

The Republican budget victory came, however, at a steep political price. The final Senate vote count of 26-to-0 was deceptive because the 23 Democrats walked out in protest before the vote. Senate minority leader Sid Snyder shocked the body by announcing his resignation Saturday to protest the way the Republicans had controlled the budget process.
"I can't stand to stay around this place anymore," said Snyder. "I have great respect for this place and it's going to hell in a handbasket."
Democrats claim the budget would not do enough to help financially-strapped school districts, workers needing job retraining, and people without health insurance.
Locke, a Democrat, has until Saturday to act on the spending plan.
Legislative leaders expect the governor to veto significant portions, if not all, of the budget, possibly forcing the legislature to go into overtime.
